primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: OTC normally combines mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate with ornithine to form citrulline. OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia; accumulated mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate spills into cytosolic pyrimidine synthesis, increasing urinary orotic acid.
vignette: A male infant becomes lethargic and vomits after initially appearing well. Laboratory studies show severe hyperammonemia, low blood urea nitrogen, low-to-normal citrulline, and increased urinary orotic acid without metabolic acidosis.
lead: Which reaction is directly impaired in this disorder?
correct: Formation of citrulline from ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate
distractors: Formation of carbamoyl phosphate from ammonia and bicarbonate in mitochondria
Conversion of citrulline to argininosuccinate in the cytosol
Cleavage of argininosuccinate to arginine and fumarate
Hydrolysis of arginine to ornithine and urea
distractor_notes: Carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase I deficiency also causes hyperammonemia but does not cause the characteristic orotic acid elevation because mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate is not generated in excess.
Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency causes citrullinemia with markedly elevated citrulline rather than the low-to-normal citrulline of OTC deficiency.
Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency produces argininosuccinic aciduria and is downstream of OTC.
Arginase deficiency blocks the final urea-cycle step and produces a different biochemical and clinical phenotype.
key_expl: Ornithine transcarbamylase catalyzes the mitochondrial reaction in which carbamoyl phosphate and ornithine form citrulline. When OTC is deficient, ammonia accumulates and excess carbamoyl phosphate is diverted into pyrimidine synthesis, producing increased orotic acid. This distinguishes OTC deficiency from carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase I deficiency.
objective: Identify the blocked ornithine-plus-carbamoyl-phosphate-to-citrulline reaction in OTC deficiency and relate it to hyperammonemia with orotic aciduria.
